# Satchel 2.0 (`satchel_20`) — spec sheet

| Class | Archetype | Durability | Base price |

| Truck | 2000s European FWD high-roof panel van, 2.0 L petrol I4, transverse engine, unibody | 3 / 5 | 20,000 |

## Design note

The parcel van on every corner: front-drive, tall and gutless, with a short first gear for pulling away loaded and not much after that. Empty it is light at the back, so it understeers safely until a sudden lift lets the rear step out — and the slab sides catch every crosswind and every shove.

## How this car breaks

Car-style unibody rather than a frame: the short nose crumples like a hatchback's and the transverse engine and radiator go early in a frontal. The cargo box behind the bulkhead is thin sheet on light hoops, so side and rear hits dent it deeply without reaching the cab. The tall body and high CG tip it in hard swerves.

## Sources (type)

- manufacturer spec-class data for 2000s European medium panel vans (petrol)
- road-test figures for the class (0-100, braking, skidpad, empty)
- engineering tables (van tire radius, ride frequency, disc/drum brake hydraulics)

All values are class-typical figures for the archetype, rounded; no single real vehicle is reproduced.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

|---|---|---|---|
| roll | 1370 | 0.85 | 1160 |
| pitch | 4515 | 0.95 | 4290 |
| yaw | 4285 | 0.97 | 4160 |

## Aerodynamics

Frontal area A = 0.88·W·H = 3.76 m²; Cd = 0.37 → **CdA = 1.392 m²**. Lift Cl·A front/rear = +0.12 / +0.10 m² (class-typical; positive = lift). No add-on aero (`aero_downforce_coeffs` = 0, mods add it).

## Engine

2.0 L SOHC 8-valve I4, multi-point injection, commercial calibration. Class-typical 2000s 2.0 L petrol van engine (~42 kW/L, ~85 kW at 5000-5500 rpm, ~176 N·m at 3000-3500) per manufacturer spec-class data: tuned for low-rev pull under load.

Peak **85 kW @ 5500 rpm**, **176 N·m @ 3000 rpm**. Idle 750 / redline 5800 / limiter 6000 rpm. Rotating inertia 0.15 kg·m² (class: 0.10 small four … 0.30 big-block). Engine braking 12% of peak torque = 21 N·m. Power-to-weight 45 kW/t.

## Drivetrain

5-speed manual, open front differential, short final drive for payload. Layout **FWD**; front diff: open; rear diff: open. Clutch capacity 1.40 × peak torque = 250 N·m. Shift time 0.35 s.

| Gear | Ratio | Overall | km/h @ redline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.73 | 16.90 | 43 |
| 2 | 2.05 | 9.29 | 78 |
| 3 | 1.32 | 5.98 | 120 |
| 4 | 0.97 | 4.39 | 164 |
| 5 | 0.76 | 3.44 | 209 |

Final drive 4.53, reverse 3.55. Speeds use the driven-wheel loaded radius 0.329 m.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.27 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 526 kg | 1.25 Hz | 32400 N/m | 2230 N·s/m | 3340 N·s/m | 0.18 m |
| Rear | 368 kg | 1.50 Hz | 32700 N/m | 1870 N·s/m | 2800 N·s/m | 0.20 m |

Round 12b ride rule (A): the file carries the derived dampers × 1.2 bump / × 1.6 rebound (rebound ≈ 2 × bump), after any tunes below: **2680 / 5340 N·s/m F, 2240 / 4480 N·s/m R** (bump / rebound).

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 5.0°/g with 65% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.653 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 139163 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 42544 F / 43424 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **18300 F / 2000 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 5.0°/g, front share 65%. Bump stops 250000 N/m.

Alignment: camber +0.0° F / +0.0° R, toe +0.00° F / +0.10° R (+ = in), caster 3.0°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 300 mm disc, pistons per side 60 mm → A = 28.3 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 125 mm, pad μ = 0.4: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.4·100 bar·28.3 cm²·0.125 m = **2827 N·m**
- Rear: 254 mm leading/trailing drum, wheel cylinder 22.2 mm → A = 3.87 cm², drum radius 127 mm, brake factor 1.8 (includes lining μ): T = BF·p·A·r = **885 N·m**

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 2540 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.11×), rear needs 520 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.69×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 580 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity exceeds that, so `bias_front` = T_r/(T_r + ideal) = **0.603** → delivered 2830 N·m front / 579 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 1930 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 17.5:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 11.9 m → outer-front path radius 5.84 m, rear-axle-centre radius 4.20 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.620 rad (35.5°)** (outer 30.9°, inner 41.5° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.70). Rack speed 1.2 rad/s.

## Damage lattice (`data/lattices/satchel_20.json`)

271 nodes, 1778 beams, 8 detachables, 21 component mounts.

- Generated with `gen-lattice --id satchel_20 --profile suv --width 1.9 --length 4.85 --height 2.25 --wheelbase 3.0 --mass 416.9 --car-mass 1895.2 --clearance 0.17 --front-overhang 0.85 --strength 1.0` (22% of vehicle mass in the lattice; strength from durability class 3).
- Era `2000s` passenger cell: 158 cabin/sill, 152 cross-member, 10 pillar, 20 roof rail → hss × 0.90 section.
- Steel hood: 105 hood beams aluminum → mild_steel.
- Detachables: steel bumpers ×2.3 break impulse / ×4 mass; steel hood ×1.4 / ×1.6.
- Cargo box: 45 Cabin nodes behind the seat partition (y < 0.08 m, just behind the front doors) relabelled FrameRear — the passenger cell is the cab only, so cargo-box hits are body damage, not cabin intrusion.
- Transverse engine: gearbox mounted on the left end of the engine block (gen-lattice places it in the tunnel at the firewall, as for FR).
